candidates.evidence_text: Motorway drivers' rush hour delays after M6/M56 interchange crash - BBC News Image source, Highways England Image caption, Motorists are facing delays after a collision on the northbound M6 in Cheshire By Angela Ferguson North West Published 27 October 2026, 07:18 GMT Updated 11 minutes ago Part of the M6 in Cheshire has been closed in both directions following a crash. Traffic England said emergency services had been called to a collision at the Lymm Interchange near Warrington, where the M6 meets junction 9 of the M56. Traffic is being diverted via the exit and entry slip roads at junction 20 and there are half-hour delays, with four miles of congestion on the approach. Traffic monitoring service Inrix said southbound M6 traffic had already built up to the Croft Interchange at junction 21. Those heading northbound can expect congestion to before junction 19 for Knutsford. Inrix said there were also delays on the M62 heading towards Manchester due to motorists trying to avoid the M6/M56 congestion. candidates.title: Coercive control victim unaware of crime until boyfriend's arrest
candidates.summary: Shannon Byrne is speaking about her ordeal because she wants to help others in a similar situation
candidates.reason: Visible repeat policy allows this item: publishable_anchor:new_phase. | Selection: Protected item selected before size limits.
candidates.practical_angle: Полиция или суд сообщили новое развитие по делу.
candidates.lead: Shannon Byrne is speaking about her ordeal because she wants to help others in a similar situation
candidates.evidence_text: Coercive control victim unaware of crime until boyfriend's arrest - BBC News Image source, Shannon Byrne Image caption, Shannon Byrne described herself as a "bubbly" person before her relationship with Declan Walsh By Lauren Hirst North West Published 26 October 2026 Shannon Byrne did not realise she had been the victim of a crime until her boyfriend was arrested and taken into custody. The now 21-year-old was sitting in the back of a police car after her family, who were concerned for her safety, had raised the alarm. "[The police officer] went through the DASH (domestic abuse, stalking and honour-based violence risk checklist) questions with me," said Shannon. "She asked me a couple of questions about his behaviour and what's the relationship like? "She just turned around and looked at me because she was sat in the front of the police car and she said 'I'm going to arrest him' and I went 'why?' "I was so confused. I said 'why are you going to arrest him?' "She said 'it's domestic violence, it's controlling and coercive behaviour'. "I understood what domestic violence was, but I didn't quite realise what controlling and coercive behaviour was at that point." Declan Walsh, 23, was arrested at his home in Stockport, Greater Manchester, on suspicion of controlling and coercive behaviour in March 2023. Image source, Shannon Byrne Image caption, Shannon, pictured with her dad following Walsh's sentencing, said it was the "best feeling ever" to give him a hug after opening up about her ordeal The couple met when Shannon was 17 and working part-time at a Costa Coffee shop, fitting in shifts around her college studies. "It was quite strange because everyone who I knew and everyone who I worked with - because he was then coming in the store so often - everyone called him my Costa stalker," she said. "He introduced himself to my dad as my Costa stalker when he first met my dad. "So it was strange because he somewhat knew his behaviour was odd but he still sort of embraced it." At first, Shannon was flattered by the attention but the relationship quickly began to spiral. She said little things built up until he was controlling her whole life, including what she wore, ate and who she spoke to. "The main tipping point for me though was going to see my nephew for his birthday and he wouldn't let me go," she said. "He's my world. I absolutely love him." After turning off the tracker on her phone, Shannon said she found the courage to tell her parents what had been happening. "[Walsh] made it out that everybody hated me and only he would love me, only he would accept me and his family," she said. "Because you have that ingrained in your brain so much, you start to believe it because it's all you hear. "So I was so scared to tell my parents what had been going on. "Not because of how they'd react or what they'd do, it's because of what he made me think they'd do." Image source, Shannon Byrne Image caption, Shannon, pictured with her mum, hopes by speaking out she will help others to come forward Shannon returned home to collect her belongings while her family waited outside. When she did not come back out, her mum called the police. Since this was her first relationship, she said she had "no idea what it should have been like". "I knew it wasn't normal, but I didn't realise it was a criminal offence," she said. "I didn't realise it was breaking the law. "I just thought I was somewhat in a bad relationship." Shannon has shared her experience to raise awareness of coercive and controlling behaviour in the hope of helping others. "I don't care what he's doing. I don't want to speak about him," said Shannon, who refuses to say his name. "It's nothing to do with that. I just want to spread awareness because it is horrible." At Stockport Magistrates' Court in July, Walsh received an eight-month custodial sentence in July, suspended for 12 months, alongside a restraining order, rehabilitation activity and unpaid work. "I want people to know that a relationship like this isn't right," said Shannon. "Nobody should control you, isolate you or make you feel worthless. "If something doesn't feel right, please speak to someone and report it. "The police helped me when I couldn't see a way out, and now I finally feel like I've got my spark back." candidates.lead: Burnham made ending rough sleeping his first pledge when entering Downing Street in July
candidates.evidence_text: Funding set to double for plan to get rough sleepers off streets by Christmas - BBC News Image source, Getty Images Image caption, The pledge was one of Burnham's key early announcements after becoming prime minister in July By Jennifer McKiernan , Political reporter and Tarah Welsh , Housing correspondent Published 25 October 2026 Updated 26 October 2026 Funding is set to double to support a pledge by the prime minister to give every rough sleeper in England a route off the streets by Christmas. Ending rough sleeping was one of Andy Burnham's first promises when he entered Downing Street, announcing a £442m package to provide emergency accommodation and practical support. Ahead of the first Rough Sleeping Summit at Downing Street on Monday, No 10 has indicated a further £432m will be added to the initiative in Wednesday's Budget. Shadow housing secretary Katie Lam said rough sleeping had hit "record highs under Labour" and criticised Burnham for failing to end rough sleeping when he was the Mayor of Greater Manchester. The most recent official figures estimated there were 4,793 people sleeping rough , external on a single night in autumn 2025 in England. The government's commitment is that every rough sleeper will either be able to physically move into accommodation by Christmas or will have been offered support as a way to prevent them sleeping rough. Money being added to the pot this week will extend support beyond March 2027 to the end of this Parliament, taking total investment to £874m. Burnham told ITV's Good Morning Britain he was confident it could be done, saying: "I have this strong feeling about putting the right standards at the heart of the country again and we can't get to a position where we just become used to walking past people sleeping rough: it's about care for people." He added: "In the end, actually, it's cheaper to do that than to leave people sleeping rough going in and out of A&E, that's not good for anybody." As Mayor of Greater Manchester, Burnham pledged to end rough sleeping in in the region by 2020, setting up the Bed Every Night scheme, which now provides more than 600 beds per night for people who might otherwise be on the streets. When he was elected in 2017 government figures showed there were 268 rough sleepers across Greater Manchester, and by 2020 that figure had more than halved to 125 - meaning Burnham missed his target. The numbers fell further to 90 in 2021, but the figures rose each year after that, reaching 197 by 2025. Asked about his previous attempts to end rough sleeping in Manchester during his time as mayor of the region, he said: "I bring the learning from that to this. "The reason why the figures went back up is because we were the only place that was offering a bed every night, so people came to Greater Manchester knowing that we were providing a higher level of support...I realised that it's only if everywhere does it at the same level that you can actually end rough sleeping." The Conservatives' Lam said: "Burnham is throwing another £432m at a problem he failed to solve in Greater Manchester." Across England, government figures show the number of people sleeping rough is at its highest level since records began in 2010. Lam said: "Under Labour, rough sleeping has hit record highs – yet their answer is always more taxpayers' money and more empty promises. "Healey must use his Budget this week to cut taxes for working people, get the ballooning benefits bill under control, and stop pushing up energy prices. "Instead of piling more costs onto hard-working people, Healey must focus on easing the cost of living and delivering real value for taxpayers' money." Burnham unveils plan to get rough sleepers off streets for Christmas Published 19 August Key takeaways as Andy Burnham becomes PM Published 20 July Burnham pledges to end rough sleeping in first speech as prime minister Published 20 July More than 30 organisations have pledged support for Burnham's plan with new partnerships, including commercial businesses and charities who attended Monday's summit. Initial funding has seen specialist outreach teams and new bed spaces operating in Coventry, with further provision being rolled out in places including Plymouth and Camden in north London over the coming weeks. The National Housing Federation will now work with housing associations to identify at least 2,000 potential homes and bed spaces, including empty properties that could be brought back into use. candidates.evidence_text: When the Golden Garter cabaret club opened its doors for the first time in October 1968, TV legend Sir Bruce Forsyth was the first name on the door Situated on a council estate in the Wythenshawe area of Manchester, people travelled from far and wide to enjoy shows at the 1,400-capacity venue From music stars Dusty Springfield, Roy Orbison and Eartha Kitt to comedians Tommy Cooper and Ronnie Corbett, there was never a shortage of acts wanting to appear "I think Dusty Springfield was the big highlight for me," said 79-year-old John Orchard, who was a pianist for Shep's Banjo Boys from 1969 to 1972 "She was my favourite singer in the 1960s and all of a sudden there she is at the Golden Garter "This is a nightclub in Wythenshawe under the flight path of the Ringway airport (now known as Manchester Airport) in the middle of the biggest council estate in Europe

candidates.evidence_text: Bradford's Reform UK council leader said he hoped to change his party's mind over its opposition to the Northern Powerhouse Rail (NPR) project Stephen Place said he was willing to make the case for the flagship rail scheme to Reform's national leadership, despite deputy leader Richard Tice previously saying his party would scrap it if the party came to power On Tuesday, the government confirmed a new station is set to be built at Bradford Interchange as part of the NPR project Speaking to the BBC's Politics North programme, Place said he was "delighted" by the new investment pledge and suggested he may need to discuss the wider stance with Tice "I just think for Bradford, as a young emerging city and a young emerging economy, we're going to need some connectivity," he said "And so, yeah, maybe I'm going to have to speak to Mr Tice and have a chat with him about it."

candidates.evidence_text: Residents in Salford are ‘fed up’ after a ‘loud and annoying’ fire alarm was again left ringing out from a rugby stadium The emergency message rang out from CorpAcq (formerly AJ Bell) Stadium from around 11pm last night, disrupting sleep and ‘drowning out the telly’, according to locals in Eccles , Swinton , and Patricroft The alarm – which repeats ’emergency, emergency’ every fifteen seconds – was caused by ‘a genuine heat sensor activation’, according to Salford Council. But it comes just three weeks after the same tannoy was left blaring for ‘tortuous four hours’ from 3am In an email to the M.E.N., one local resident, Caroline said: “The emergency evacuation tannoy loop has been blaring continuously overnight, keeping residents awake across the local area.” She claimed when trying to contact Salford Council, who own the stadium, on their emergency out-of-hours number, ‘the operator flatly refused to log the incident or send anyone out’ “Given that Salford City Council is owner of this stadium asset, it is a complete failure of duty that their own emergency teams are passing the buck while local tax-paying residents suffer through the night,” she added

candidates.evidence_text: Courts Woman died after pulling over to check on driver who had crashed on M60, trial hears Ahmed Qasim denies causing death by dangerous driving Add to preferred sources News Andrew Bardsley Court reporter 18:16, 26 Oct 2026 View 2 Images Ahmed Qasim A woman died after being hit by a speeding car which lost control on the M60 minutes after she’d pulled over to check on a driver who had crashed, a trial has heard Rachel Gwynne, 38, became ‘sandwiched’ between two cars and had to have one of her legs amputated. She died weeks later after suffering a blood clot She had been driving a Citroen Dispatch van and pulled over between junction 23 of the M60 clockwise at Ashton-under-Lyne and junction 24 at Denton. She had witnessed David Wigmore’s Ford Fiesta which ‘aquaplaned’ across all four lanes of the motorway, smash into the crash barrie Wigmore, then 30, had been driving ‘too fast’ and in excess of the 70mph speed limit, Minshull Street Crown Court heard. Ms Gwynne and her two passengers had got out to check on Wigmore, who was not hurt but ‘shaken up’ Ms Gwynne, who was using the van to move home, was then hit by a BMW which was also speeding and lost control. The car was driven by Ahmed Qasim, 39, who had been driving to Manchester Airport to pick up his wife

candidates.evidence_text: Bury It has been a police station, a courthouse and a school, now it could be new homes 100 years of history has taken place in these buildings Add to preferred sources Comments News Hannah Richardson 14:36, 26 Oct 2026 View 2 Images The former Bury G Buildings which once formed part of Bury Grammar School could now get a new lease of life Plans have been submitted to Bury council to convert part of the old school estate into new homes. The three buildings, in Tenterden Street, Bury, currently stand empty after being vacated by the school when it ‘rationalised and expanded’ its estate The premises are thought to date back to around 1927 when they served as a police station and courthouse. The site was bought by the Bury Grammar School in 1993, and was initially used as a junior boys’ school. Later, it became a sixth form centre Developer Property Investment Complete Ltd has now put forward proposals to convert what were the Main School Building, Arts Building and Sixth Form Building into new homes . Some 21 apartments are suggested for the site Of these, 14 could be created in the main building, two in the arts centre and five in the sixth form building. Add-ons are also proposed for the latter two buildings which would see the existing single-storey extensions increased to two storeys

candidates.evidence_text: Manchester Council Collyhurst woman, 63, trapped on seventh floor of her tower block and unable to leave for months "It's been a total and utter farce" Add to preferred sources Comments News Ramazani Mwamba News reporter 05:55, 27 Oct 2026 Updated 06: A 63-year-old woman has been trapped on the seventh floor of a Manchester tower block for almost four months. Sian Anderson, who requires the use of a wheelchair, has been unable to leave her flat in Humphries Court, Collyhurst, since July when the lift she uses to come and go br It has left her unable to attend scheduled appointments, her carer, Philip Anderson, told the Manchester Evening News Philip, who is also Sian's younger brother, explained that Sian is wheelchair dependant after she suffered two strokes in 2020 and 2021. He says his sister's ordeal of becoming imprisoned in her own home began on July 7 "July 7 was the last time Sian was able to leave the building," said Philip. "Because obviously no lift, she can't use the stairs "She's had to cancel multiple medical appointments and now we've been told by the council that the lift won't be done until possibly December."

candidates.evidence_text: Bury Bury teacher banned from profession for life after conviction for historic sex offences William Nulty was convicted of nine offences said to have taken place when he was a teenager Add to preferred sources Comments News Greta Simpson Senior Repor A teacher working at a Bury primary school has been banned from the profession for life after being convicted of historic sex offences he committed as a teenager William Nulty, 32, maintained his innocence after being handed a suspended sentence for the offences, telling a teaching panel he was 'trying to recover from trauma' and wished 'for the matter to be resolved as quickly and privately as possible' He had been a teacher at the Our Lady of Lourdes primary school in Bury when the allegations were first made in July 2022, and had been suspended and then dismissed by the end of September that year, according to a professional conduct panel outcome published by the Teaching Regu After a police investigation, Mr Nulty was convicted in 2025 of nine counts of historic sexual offences against a girl under 13 between 2010 and 2012, when he was aged between 16 and 18, the report said After being handed a suspended sentence, he has now been banned indefinitely from the profession, with no provision for a future review period

candidates.evidence_text: Residents in Salford are ‘fed up’ after a ‘loud and annoying’ fire alarm was again left ringing out from a rugby stadium The emergency message rang out from CorpAcq (formerly AJ Bell) Stadium from around 11pm last night, disrupting sleep and ‘drowning out the telly’, according to locals in Eccles , Swinton , and Patricroft The alarm – which repeats ’emergency, emergency’ every fifteen seconds – was caused by ‘a genuine heat sensor activation’, according to Salford Council. But it comes just three weeks after the same tannoy was left blaring for ‘tortuous four hours’ from 3am In an email to the M.E.N., one local resident, Caroline said: “The emergency evacuation tannoy loop has been blaring continuously overnight, keeping residents awake across the local area.” She claimed when trying to contact Salford Council, who own the stadium, on their emergency out-of-hours number, ‘the operator flatly refused to log the incident or send anyone out’ “Given that Salford City Council is owner of this stadium asset, it is a complete failure of duty that their own emergency teams are passing the buck while local tax-paying residents suffer through the night,” she added

Add to preferred sources Comments News Declan Carey Local Democracy Reporter 19:0 People using Greater Manchester’s tips will need to prove they live in the region under new rules being introduced in 2027 - despite fears from a councillor that it could lead to long ‘passport-style’ queues The new checks will be rolled out from New Year according to a Greater Manchester Combined Authority (GMCA) report, apart from in Wigan which is not part of the region’s waste disposal authority It means anyone trying to dump rubbish at a tip will need to show a driver’s licence or other type of document confirming they live at a local address The move comes amid fears that dump closures in neighbouring counties are pushing people to travel to Greater Manchester and use its recycling centres for free The GMCA report about the new rules stated that the change is expected to begin from New Year 2027, with an initial ‘soft’ launch

candidates.evidence_text: Tameside Hospital 'If Dad can't come, I'm going to hospital in my wedding dress' Sinead Jackson took part of her wedding day to a Greater Manchester hospital ward after her dad unexpectedly fell ill Add to preferred sources Comments News Bethan Finigh A bride who was left 'heartbroken' after her dad was rushed to hospital before her wedding day made sure he could still share in her big day by visiting the ward in her wedding dress Sinead Jackson, 36, was due to marry her partner Stephen at the Village Hotel in Hyde on October 10 when her dad, Leslie Healy, was admitted to Tameside Hospital with heart problems Leslie was told by medics on the hospital's acute cardiology unit (ACU) he was too unwell to attend the wedding, leaving Sinead devastated at the thought of missing out on the moment she had always dreamed of - having her dad walk her down the aisle Sinead, who lives in Dukinfield, who had been waiting weeks for her dad to see her in her wedding dress, visited him on the ward alongside her wedding photographer, Jen, with the help of staff on the ACU View 6 Images Sinead visited Tameside hospital's acute cardiology unit before walking down the aisle (Image: Tameside and Glossop Integrated Care)

candidates.evidence_text: Courts Woman died after pulling over to check on driver who had crashed on M60, trial hears Ahmed Qasim denies causing death by dangerous driving Add to preferred sources News Andrew Bardsley Court reporter 18:16, 26 Oct 2026 View 2 Images Ahmed Qasim A woman died after being hit by a speeding car which lost control on the M60 minutes after she’d pulled over to check on a driver who had crashed, a trial has heard Rachel Gwynne, 38, became ‘sandwiched’ between two cars and had to have one of her legs amputated. She died weeks later after suffering a blood clot She had been driving a Citroen Dispatch van and pulled over between junction 23 of the M60 clockwise at Ashton-under-Lyne and junction 24 at Denton. She had witnessed David Wigmore’s Ford Fiesta which ‘aquaplaned’ across all four lanes of the motorway, smash into the crash barrie Wigmore, then 30, had been driving ‘too fast’ and in excess of the 70mph speed limit, Minshull Street Crown Court heard. Ms Gwynne and her two passengers had got out to check on Wigmore, who was not hurt but ‘shaken up’ Ms Gwynne, who was using the van to move home, was then hit by a BMW which was also speeding and lost control. The car was driven by Ahmed Qasim, 39, who had been driving to Manchester Airport to pick up his wife

candidates.evidence_text: Salford Police descend on Salford flat block with woman 'critical' in hospital Officers were called to the scene at Malus Court in Pendleton on Sunday afternoon Add to preferred sources News Ashlie Blakey Live and breaking news reporter 10:13, 26 Oct A woman was rushed to hospital in a critical condition after emergency crews were called to a flat block in Salford Police and paramedics descended on the scene at Malus Court, on Belvedere Road in the Pendleton area, at around 2.40pm on Sunday (October 25). Crews responded to reports of a 'concern for the welfare of a woman' The woman was rushed to hospital by paramedics. She remains there in a critical condition, a spokesperson for Greater Manchester Police said Amid the incident, two men, aged 54 and 58, were arrested. They were both arrested on suspicion of being concerned in the supply of class A drugs. The 54-year-old man was further arrested on suspicion of racially/religiously aggravated harassment GMP has not revealed any further information on the incident. Residents reported seeing a large police presence in the area on Sunday afternoon, with a police car reportedly remaining on the scene overnight and into this morning (Monday)

Following a foot chase and nearby searches, they discovered a 17-year-old boy hiding inside a wheelie bin Bodycam footage shared by the force shows an officer shining a torch on a green wheelie bin laid on the ground, from which a pair of feet can be seen protruding. "Out you come now," the officer is heard to shout The boy was arrested on suspicion of burglary, with another 16-year-old girl arrested on suspicion of attempted burglary View Image The moment cops in Bolton found a teen suspect hiding in a wheelie bin after an alleged burglary. candidates.lead: Bury It has been a police station, a courthouse and a school, now it could be new homes 100 years of history has taken place in these buildings Add to preferred sources Comments News Hannah Richardson 14:36, 26 Oct 2026 View 2 Images The former Bury G Buildings which once formed
candidates.evidence_text: Bury It has been a police station, a courthouse and a school, now it could be new homes 100 years of history has taken place in these buildings Add to preferred sources Comments News Hannah Richardson 14:36, 26 Oct 2026 View 2 Images The former Bury G Buildings which once formed part of Bury Grammar School could now get a new lease of life Plans have been submitted to Bury council to convert part of the old school estate into new homes. The three buildings, in Tenterden Street, Bury, currently stand empty after being vacated by the school when it ‘rationalised and expanded’ its estate The premises are thought to date back to around 1927 when they served as a police station and courthouse. The site was bought by the Bury Grammar School in 1993, and was initially used as a junior boys’ school. Later, it became a sixth form centre Developer Property Investment Complete Ltd has now put forward proposals to convert what were the Main School Building, Arts Building and Sixth Form Building into new homes . Some 21 apartments are suggested for the site Of these, 14 could be created in the main building, two in the arts centre and five in the sixth form building. Add-ons are also proposed for the latter two buildings which would see the existing single-storey extensions increased to two storeys

Sian Anderson, who requires the use of a wheelchair, has been unable to leave her flat in Humphries Court, Collyhurst, since July when the lift she uses to come and go br It has left her unable to attend scheduled appointments, her carer, Philip Anderson, told the Manchester Evening News Philip, who is also Sian's younger brother, explained that Sian is wheelchair dependant after she suffered two strokes in 2020 and 2021. He says his sister's ordeal of becoming imprisoned in her own home began on July 7 "July 7 was the last time Sian was able to leave the building," said Philip. "Because obviously no lift, she can't use the stairs "She's had to cancel multiple medical appointments and now we've been told by the council that the lift won't be done until possibly December."

candidates.evidence_text: Bury Bury teacher banned from profession for life after conviction for historic sex offences William Nulty was convicted of nine offences said to have taken place when he was a teenager Add to preferred sources Comments News Greta Simpson Senior Repor A teacher working at a Bury primary school has been banned from the profession for life after being convicted of historic sex offences he committed as a teenager William Nulty, 32, maintained his innocence after being handed a suspended sentence for the offences, telling a teaching panel he was 'trying to recover from trauma' and wished 'for the matter to be resolved as quickly and privately as possible' He had been a teacher at the Our Lady of Lourdes primary school in Bury when the allegations were first made in July 2022, and had been suspended and then dismissed by the end of September that year, according to a professional conduct panel outcome published by the Teaching Regu After a police investigation, Mr Nulty was convicted in 2025 of nine counts of historic sexual offences against a girl under 13 between 2010 and 2012, when he was aged between 16 and 18, the report said After being handed a suspended sentence, he has now been banned indefinitely from the profession, with no provision for a future review period

candidates.lead: Residents in Salford are ‘fed up’ after a ‘loud and annoying’ fire alarm was again left ringing out from a rugby stadium The emergency message rang out from CorpAcq (formerly AJ Bell) Stadium from around 11pm last night, disrupting sleep and ‘drowning out the telly’, according to
candidates.evidence_text: Residents in Salford are ‘fed up’ after a ‘loud and annoying’ fire alarm was again left ringing out from a rugby stadium The emergency message rang out from CorpAcq (formerly AJ Bell) Stadium from around 11pm last night, disrupting sleep and ‘drowning out the telly’, according to locals in Eccles , Swinton , and Patricroft The alarm – which repeats ’emergency, emergency’ every fifteen seconds – was caused by ‘a genuine heat sensor activation’, according to Salford Council. But it comes just three weeks after the same tannoy was left blaring for ‘tortuous four hours’ from 3am In an email to the M.E.N., one local resident, Caroline said: “The emergency evacuation tannoy loop has been blaring continuously overnight, keeping residents awake across the local area.” She claimed when trying to contact Salford Council, who own the stadium, on their emergency out-of-hours number, ‘the operator flatly refused to log the incident or send anyone out’ “Given that Salford City Council is owner of this stadium asset, it is a complete failure of duty that their own emergency teams are passing the buck while local tax-paying residents suffer through the night,” she added

candidates.evidence_text: Greater Manchester Combined Authority New rule coming to Greater Manchester tips sparks fear of ‘passport-style’ queues A new report has been published about the change. Add to preferred sources Comments News Declan Carey Local Democracy Reporter 19:0 People using Greater Manchester’s tips will need to prove they live in the region under new rules being introduced in 2027 - despite fears from a councillor that it could lead to long ‘passport-style’ queues The new checks will be rolled out from New Year according to a Greater Manchester Combined Authority (GMCA) report, apart from in Wigan which is not part of the region’s waste disposal authority It means anyone trying to dump rubbish at a tip will need to show a driver’s licence or other type of document confirming they live at a local address The move comes amid fears that dump closures in neighbouring counties are pushing people to travel to Greater Manchester and use its recycling centres for free The GMCA report about the new rules stated that the change is expected to begin from New Year 2027, with an initial ‘soft’ launch

candidates.evidence_text: Tameside Hospital 'If Dad can't come, I'm going to hospital in my wedding dress' Sinead Jackson took part of her wedding day to a Greater Manchester hospital ward after her dad unexpectedly fell ill Add to preferred sources Comments News Bethan Finigh A bride who was left 'heartbroken' after her dad was rushed to hospital before her wedding day made sure he could still share in her big day by visiting the ward in her wedding dress Sinead Jackson, 36, was due to marry her partner Stephen at the Village Hotel in Hyde on October 10 when her dad, Leslie Healy, was admitted to Tameside Hospital with heart problems Leslie was told by medics on the hospital's acute cardiology unit (ACU) he was too unwell to attend the wedding, leaving Sinead devastated at the thought of missing out on the moment she had always dreamed of - having her dad walk her down the aisle Sinead, who lives in Dukinfield, who had been waiting weeks for her dad to see her in her wedding dress, visited him on the ward alongside her wedding photographer, Jen, with the help of staff on the ACU View 6 Images Sinead visited Tameside hospital's acute cardiology unit before walking down the aisle (Image: Tameside and Glossop Integrated Care)

candidates.summary: Bury It has been a police station, a courthouse and a school, now it could be new homes 100 years of history has taken place in these buildings Add to preferred sources Comments News Hannah Richardson 14:36, 26 Oct 2026 View 2 Images The former Bury G Buildings which once formed

candidates.lead: Bury It has been a police station, a courthouse and a school, now it could be new homes 100 years of history has taken place in these buildings Add to preferred sources Comments News Hannah Richardson 14:36, 26 Oct 2026 View 2 Images The former Bury G Buildings which once formed
candidates.evidence_text: Bury It has been a police station, a courthouse and a school, now it could be new homes 100 years of history has taken place in these buildings Add to preferred sources Comments News Hannah Richardson 14:36, 26 Oct 2026 View 2 Images The former Bury G Buildings which once formed part of Bury Grammar School could now get a new lease of life Plans have been submitted to Bury council to convert part of the old school estate into new homes. The three buildings, in Tenterden Street, Bury, currently stand empty after being vacated by the school when it ‘rationalised and expanded’ its estate The premises are thought to date back to around 1927 when they served as a police station and courthouse. The site was bought by the Bury Grammar School in 1993, and was initially used as a junior boys’ school. Later, it became a sixth form centre Developer Property Investment Complete Ltd has now put forward proposals to convert what were the Main School Building, Arts Building and Sixth Form Building into new homes . Some 21 apartments are suggested for the site Of these, 14 could be created in the main building, two in the arts centre and five in the sixth form building. Add-ons are also proposed for the latter two buildings which would see the existing single-storey extensions increased to two storeys

The Boeing 737-800 flight RYR56QH issued the 7700 squawk code approximately 20 minutes before touching down at the airport The code indicates a general emergency, and it has since been confirmed that a passenger had taken ill during the journey. According to Flight Radar, the plane touched down in Manchester at 11.30pm View 2 Images The emergency was declared just before landing (Image: Squawk)

candidates.evidence_text: Councillor Pat Karney 'I couldn't deal with fire in my mouth': How losing his mum inspired Pat Karney's crusade to ban smoking Following the death of Cllr Pat Karney aged 78, John Scheerhout examines the personal tragedy that drove one of his greatest Add to preferred sources News John Scheerhout Crime reporter 17:21, 25 Oct 2026 Updated 06:22, 26 Oct 2026 Pat Karney watched his beloved mother Mary die of smoking-related illness. The late Labour veteran possessed an ingrained sense of public duty but perhaps it was this intens For years before smoking in pubs and restaurants was eventually outlawed in England in 2007, he was the passionate leader for a campaign to make Manchester smoke-free. Of course, he believed his adopted home city of Manchester should always be first His late mother had been seduced into addiction by images of the glamorous Hollywood greats, puffing away on the silver screen. So in 2004 he resolved to do something about a public health crisis which was blighting Manchester more than anywhere else in the country He had tried smoking at London School of Economics where he got a BSc in politics and economics and even tried a joint on a trip to Amsterdam but disliked it immediately. He admitted he 'couldn't deal with having a fire in my mouth' His campaigning went through many ups and downs but ended in victory, and probably helped to save lives. He died earlier this month, aged 78

Simon Richardson, 35, denies murdering Michael Mullins View 9 Images Add to preferred sources New Simon Richardson, 35, struck Mr Mullins in his Volvo in Altrincham in April, at the junction of Dunham Road and Warburton Lane, a jury was told. The 56-year-old was making his way home to Northwich from work, it was said It is alleged that Mr Richardson failed to properly observe the junction, 'flying straight through the give-way markers', before hitting Mr Mullins Minshull Street Crown Court heard that Mr Richardson 'put his foot down', as Mr Mullins was trapped under the car, while his damaged bike was left in the road He was dragged under the wheels of the car for 1.3 miles - 2.2km - before dying at the roadside on Wet Gate Lane in Lymm, it was said. Prosecutors allege that Mr Richardson later stopped, got out of the car and made 'concerted physical efforts' to try and pull Mr Mullins out from He then carried on driving, veering 'sharply and deliberately' from side to side and mounting a grass verge. Witnesses followed a trail of blood in the road before finding Mr Mullins fatally injured. He was pronounced dead at the scene

candidates.evidence_text: Why Britain's top-performing police chief is being forced out - and his warning to the Home Office Following a leaked letter exposing a bitter rift with PCC Dan Price over his contract, retiring Cheshire Chief Constable Mark Roberts speaks to the M.E. Add to preferred sources Comments News Neal Keeling Chief reporter 15:57, 25 Oct 2026 There is bit of old cross-county banter between Greater Manchester and Cheshire Police which Mark Roberts is familiar with. GMP would refer to their more rural neighbours as "The Gurkhas" - beca During his five and a half years tenure as Chief Constable of Cheshire Constabulary Roberts has made sure the joke is well and truly redundant The force is currently one of the best performing in the country according to His Majesty Inspectorate of Constabularies. A sweet fact for Roberts as his policing career began on the streets of Manchester and Salford This year Cheshire ranked top nationally for crime outcome rates, high charge/summons rates, and excellence in tackling violence, burglary, and sexual offences It therefore begs the question why after a 33-year stellar career he is choosing to retire early. He is due to leave the force on November 5th. But he had hoped to negotiate an extension to his contract which would have taken him to 2028

Credit: UK Parliament A Labour MP has revealed that she is a victim of domestic abuse - Speaking in the Commons on October 13, Kirith Entwistle, who represents Bolton North East, described her experience of the current court system as "triggering", adding that she had to watch her abuser "stare at her" during a recent video hearing Ms Entwistle told her fellow MPs that she believes special measures - where victims are given protection or assistance in court - should be the standard in cases involving domestic abuse Examples of these measures could include screens, the ability to give evidence through a live link, or witnesses being able to be accompanied when giving evidence Measures to protect victims are included in the Courts and Tribunals Bill, which is currently going through Parliament Speaking during a debate on the bill, Ms Entwistle said: "It doesn’t matter how many times somebody tells me that they understand what I’m going through, or they acknowledge what I’ve been through, they really don’t unless they have lived it themselves or know somebody who has."

candidates.evidence_text: Bolton Council is one of at least four local authorities who have refused to accept the government's latest planning changes. Credit: PNW Four local authorities have drawn lines in the sand, refusing to amend their constitutions to adopt the latest statutory government guidance that would see officers become the default body for deciding most planning applications across England Bolton Council, Tameside Council, Central Bedfordshire Council, and Fenland Council have refused to amend their constitutions to be compliant with the National Scheme of Delegation of Planning Functions, which goes into effect on 1 November Their decision will inevitably have consequences, should they continue to refuse to comply In short, the regulation changes mean that more applications will be decided by officers and less by committees This will create a national standard for what is, and what is not, taken to council planning committees – whereas previously local authorities could set their own guidelines for what sort of application merited the committee treatment

candidates.evidence_text: How a sweatshop empire is Manchester-washing its reputation “I can’t always be in LA,” reads one TikTok caption, “someone has to hold it down in Rochdale.” It’s written over a model strutting through a leatherwear shoot. She’s wearing Musera, which looks to be Manchester’s friendliest, chicest new clothing label — launched in 2024 from an From this Newton Street office, a band of young designers turn out a stream of trend pieces: low-rise trousers and asymmetric tops, distressed knitwear and leopard-print flares, western fringed jumpers and A-level prom gowns. Their Instagram bio lauds the brand as “Est. MCR.” Over a million people watched the staff dancing around their Northern Quarter office to Whigfield’s Saturday Night on TikTok. More still tuned in to a video showing them kitted out in Musera for Drake’s performance at Co-op Live last year. And who knows how many have sidestepped “Be a muse in your own era,” goes their slogan; presumably also the source of their similarly recondite name. Their Instagram captions are a list of internet cliches verging on parody. “My blood type is iced latte,” reads one post Looking at this well-curated online presence, you might well be convinced that Musera is, as they suggest, Manchester through and through

candidates.evidence_text: An 'unparalleled' investigation shows a third of staff surveyed have experienced bad behaviour from senior officials A scathing report into Manchester City Council's working culture has found a prevailing “boys' club” mentality and widespread bad behaviour by senior staff. The internal document – that will be shared with council workers tomorrow and is based on a survey of nearly 1,200 staff – The report describes a culture at the council in which senior staff can act inappropriately with seeming impunity. Many junior staff members believe raising issues will lead to retaliation, and 59% of survey respondents have witnessed or experienced a form of harassment, discrimi One worker recalled a young apprentice being repeatedly sexually harassed by a senior colleague until she was forced to leave the council. “He was allowed to stay,” they said of the offending staffer. “She was interviewed by two male managers and needless to say she left.” There A council worker, speaking to us on the condition of anonymity, said of the report: “if I were a manager that would sicken me to my core.” When we approached the council before publishing this story, CEO Tom Stannard said: “it is completely unacceptable that anyone should feel undervalued, unable to raise concerns, unsupported if they do or – in the worst cases – unsafe. These issues cannot and will not be ignored.”

candidates.lead: A public consultation has opened on changes that could affect who secures one of the sought-after grammar school's 204 Year 7 places
candidates.evidence_text: A public consultation has opened on changes that could affect who secures one of the sought-after grammar school's 204 Year 7 places Share on WhatsApp Share via Email Girls living close to Altrincham Grammar School for Girls could lose priority for places to children attending four designated primary schools under proposed changes to its admissions policy A public consultation has opened on plans to give pupils from four primary schools belonging to the same academy trust as AGGS priority over other applicants who have passed the entrance examination – even if they live closer to the school The proposals, which would take effect from September 2028, could have significant implications for Altrincham families whose daughters attend local primary schools outside Bright Futures Educational Trust Under the existing admissions system, girls who pass the entrance examination and live within the school's eight-mile catchment area are generally prioritised according to how close they live to AGGS, after higher-priority categories have been considered But the proposed arrangements would introduce a new category giving preference to qualifying pupils attending four primary schools within Bright Futures Educational Trust

candidates.source_evidence: Manchester hospitals have become a focal point not only for improving people’s health but supporting them overcome financial or housing challenges In December 2023 a trial was launched to embed two Citizens Advice case workers in two Manchester University NHS Foundation Trust (MFT) run hospitals in Manchester - the Royal Manchester Children's Hospital and North Manchester General Hospital This was further expanded in June 2024 to include Wythenshawe Hospital, and the MRI in March 2025, and St Mary's in December 2025 with funding through MFT’s charity, as well as a damp and mould focused case worker funded through Manchester City Council The team of six Citizens Advice caseworkers are aimed at providing better wrap around care for patients and addressing the link we know exists between poor health, economic hardship and housing issues The trial has been a huge success with more than 1,500 people supported across the trial locations With more up to 3m patients contacts across MFT each year this presented a huge opportunity to reach people who may otherwise have not known about the services provided by Citizens Advice, or the support they were eligible to claim

candidates.evidence_text: Rochdale Town Hall’s Martlet Kitchen has picked up the Trip Advisor Travellers’ Choice Award 2026, placing it among the top-rated restaurants in the world on the popular review site The award honours businesses which consistently receive great reviews, with their scores placing them in the top 10 per cent of all establishments registered on the popular review site With millions of businesses from around the globe listed on the site, the award is a huge accolade for the Martlet Kitchen, which recently celebrated its second birthday It’s not the first time the restaurant, which specialises in traditional, high-quality British food, has been lauded In his food column for The Guardian, legendary food critic Jay Rayner, described the Martlet Kitchen as a ‘victory of professionalism, good sense and, most of all, great taste and skill’ when he visited shortly after its opening in 2024 The Martlet Kitchen is helmed by multi award winning chef, Darren Parkinson, who trained at Hopwood Hall College before working at acclaimed establishments including Shibden Mill Inn in Halifax and the Fleece Inn in Ripponden, both of which boast 2 AA rosettes

english_fact_card.why_now: The figures were released during Stoptober, an annual campaign encouraging people to quit smoking.

candidates.lead: Experience the raw, unfiltered power of Balkan folklore in a new immersive show from the world’s most famous performance artist Balkan Erotic Epic is a bold new performance work created by the iconic artist Marina Abramović .
candidates.evidence_text: Experience the raw, unfiltered power of Balkan folklore in a new immersive show from the world’s most famous performance artist Balkan Erotic Epic is a bold new performance work created by the iconic artist Marina Abramović . Regarded as the world’s most influential performance artist, Abramović’s transformative work has reached millions of people – from opening the Pyramid Stage at Glastonbury Festival t A four-hour ritual where ancient myth meets performance art, Balkan Erotic Epic explores the eroticism, spirituality and traditions of Abramović’s homeland through 13 visceral scenes Brought to life by a cast of over 70 performers, dancers, musicians and singers, the experience unfolds across Aviva Studios. Audiences are free to choose their own path – with pop-up encounters punctuating the action, bringing bodies together in dance, song and ritual Watch Fertility Rite , a fevered ritual where bodies writhe against the ground in a desperate call for fertility. Witness Massaging the Breast where women gesticulate over graves to awaken the earth. In Scaring the Gods , women bare themselves to the sky to banish storms. Listen Unafraid to push the boundaries of eroticism and performance art, Balkan Erotic Epic asks its audience a timeless question: What are our bodies truly for?

History, power and empire collide in Button Up! – a major new exhibition from the world-leading artist and activist Ai Weiwei . Internationally renowned artist and activist Ai Weiwei turns his critical gaze to the last 200 years of global history with this major new exhibition. Monumental in scale and ambition, Ai Weiwei: Button Up! is the artist’s most expansive presentation in the North to date.. Ai Weiwei is known around the world for his uncompromising artistic vision and political activism. From a childhood in exile to surviving secret detention in China, his remarkable life and career have led him to global prominence. Using sculpture, installation, film, photography and architecture, his work is unafraid to ask urgent, critical questions.. In Button Up! , the artist turns his lens on two centuries of Chinese and British relations. Taking inspiration from Manchester, a city at the heart of the Industrial Revolution, Button Up! explores how historic systems of trade, empire and exploitation resonate in today’s humanitarian and political crises.. Conceived as a total environment, Ai Weiwei: Button Up! brings together new and existing large-scale works on display in the UK for the first time. The monumental installation features porcelain, cotton, glass, bronze and even buttons and toy bricks. Each material contains a story of human invention and consumption. Together, they paint a picture of globalisation.. Both global and personal, the title Button Up! is a playful poke at the artist’s ongoing battle with censorship. The exhibition also features the world premiere of a new body of work created especially for the vast spaces of the Warehouse – Eight-Nation Alliance Flags made from millions of buttons, as well as a new version of History Of Bombs made entirely from toy bricks.. The new commissions sit alongside large-scale works by the artist which are going on show in the UK for the first time: Law of the Journey (2017), a 47m long inflatable migrant boat containing hundreds of human figures and the artist’s largest artwork to date; Wang Family Ancestral Hall (2015), a Ming dynasty ancestral temple reassembled from 1,500 individual wooden pieces ; and La Commedia Umana (2017-21), a black Murano glass chandelier made up of over 2,000 pieces and weighing nearly 3 tonnes. Also on show is Circle of Animals/Zodiac Heads (2010), a re-envisioning of the twelve animals of the Chinese zodiac.. Button Up! immerses visitors in Ai Weiwei’s fearless interrogation of the forces past and present that drive today’s injustices – while championing art’s enduring power to challenge and inspire.. . . . “I’m not interested in making very big things just for the sake of it. But in Manchester, that wonderful Warehouse space calls for monumental work. Visiting the city for this exhibition – the birthplace of the Industrial Revolution – and reflecting on Britain’s global territorial expansion made me realise I had to explore that history and understand how it connects to the forces driving today’s wars and global crises. The world today is deeply divided, with tragedy all around. Understanding history goes hand in hand with standing up for truth and justice.”. Ai Weiwei. . . Explore. . Ai Weiwei | Dream Space . candidates.evidence_text: Finish work and unwind with live music from Manchester’s best jazz musicians. Beat the Jams live series showcases the very best of the jazz scene, at short rush hour gigs from 6pm at Band on the Wall. What better way to avoid those endless queues, chaotic traffic and stressful homeward journeys? Clock off and skip the rush-hour traffic while you watch live jazz and make the most of our happy hour deals from 5–7pm: £4.50 pints / 2 for £15 cocktails / £15 bottles of wine + pizzas from £5! The new season kicks off on 24 September with tenor saxophonist Dean Masser and pianist Richard Wetherall, followed by: 7 October – Anna Chandler-King Quartet Leeds based saxophonist and composer Anna joins us again for Beat the Jams, this time with her own band. Anna’s thoughtful and inventive compositions are firm favourites of us at Beat the Jams and her quartet promises to be a unique rush hour busting treat! 16 November – Sam Lightwing Quartet Saxophonist and composer Sam Lightwing brings presents brand new music for his thrilling young quartet, showcasing Sam’s original compositions, which blend classic mainstream jazz grooves with modern flavours of post-pop and latin, all wrapped up in the language of contemporary sax giants such as Chris Potter, Seamus Blake and Joshua Redman. 15 December – Svarc/Devine/Walsh with Richard Iles The band combines deep pocket, fearless interplay and a shared love of exploration. Expect everything from soulful melodies and infectious rhythms to moments of exhilarating collective improvisation, delivered with the chemistry that only world-class musicians can create. Tickets from £13 per show, or £42 for a season ticket

Clock off and skip the rush-hour traffic while you watch live jazz and make the most of our happy hour deals from 5–7pm: £4.50 pints / 2 for £15 cocktails / £15 bottles of wine + pizzas from £5! The new season kicks off on 24 September with tenor saxophonist Dean Masser and pianist Richard Wetherall, followed by: 7 October – Anna Chandler-King Quartet Leeds based saxophonist and composer Anna joins us again for Beat the Jams, this time with her own band. Anna’s thoughtful and inventive compositions are firm favourites of us at Beat the Jams and her quartet promises to be a unique rush hour busting treat! 16 November – Sam Lightwing Quartet Saxophonist and composer Sam Lightwing brings presents brand new music for his thrilling young quartet, showcasing Sam’s original compositions, which blend classic mainstream jazz grooves with modern flavours of post-pop and latin, all wrapped up in the language of contemporary sax giants such as Chris Potter, Seamus Blake and Joshua Redman. 15 December – Svarc/Devine/Walsh with Richard Iles The band combines deep pocket, fearless interplay and a shared love of exploration. Expect everything from soulful melodies and infectious rhythms to moments of exhilarating collective improvisation, delivered with the chemistry that only world-class musicians can create. Tickets from £13 per show, or £42 for a season ticket

candidates.lead: Mr Thomas’s Chop House has been part of Manchester since 1867.
candidates.evidence_text: Mr Thomas’s Chop House has been part of Manchester since 1867. A £300,000 restoration, long-term lease and 23-year-old head chef are shaping what comes next Go to Manchester's Finest X profile Mr Thomas’s Chop House has been serving Manchester since 1867, but owner Roger Ward admits there was a point after Covid when he wasn’t sure how much longer he wanted to keep doing it Tom’s had gone eight years without a proper lease and much longer without any meaningful investment by the landlord. Retirement was being seriously considered. Instead, Roger decided to “go again properly” That decision has resulted in a new long-term commitment to the Chop Houses and around £300,000 being spent restoring Tom’s – touching everything from the dining rooms and furniture to the menu, wine list, kitchen and beer cellars Roger is particularly pleased with the toilets “Tom’s was famous for the shittest toilets in town,” he says. They are now, by his assessment, considerably less so. Downstairs has been redone, upstairs has new ones too, while a previously overlooked back room has been completely reworked

The opening marks Open Restaurant Group’s 9th restaurant to date and its second site in Greater Manchester, following the launch of Arcadian in Di At the heart of the restaurant will be a four-to-five-seat chef’s counter, placing guests directly at the pass for an up-close view of the kitchen in action. At Counter, he challenges convention by exploring what British cooking can The menu puts this philosophy into practice with dishes that combine unexpected ingredients and inventive flavour pairings. Highlights include the Beef Tartare Pressed Croissant, pairing aged beef with a crispy pressed croissant, smoked oyster mayo, wasabi and pickled shallot; th From the grill, guests can expect the Satay Spatchcock Chicken, served with peanut satay, fermented chilli, coconut, burnt lime and crispy shallo t, alongside Turbot Steak, a bone-in cut finished with brown butter, green chilli and preserved lemon

candidates.evidence_text: Red Light, Manchester’s award-winning LGBTQ+ cocktail bar, is making a surprise return to the city on Friday 9th October Reopening on Tariff Street in the heart of the Northern Quarter (next door to The Whisky Jar), the beloved venue reopens with a seductive new aesthetic, an expanded food and drink offering, and a revived music program Founded by Deana Ferguson, Red Light’s new home delivers the original concept fully realised: a refined yet welcoming sanctuary blending sleek booth seating, striking red lights, a bar, boutique club vibes, and an outdoor terrace open until 11 PM. The interior showcases the works The famous cocktail menu will return, featuring favourites like the Pink Picante, Pomme Verte – a popular twist on an appletini, Belfast Coffee, the famous spicy pickle martini Especiado and the Pornstar Chic, crafted with homemade passionfruit sorbet Red Light also introduces a brand-new savoury snack menu, including, Boquerones, Pickled Guindilla peppers, Gordal olives, Mini Croissant Butter Blondies from Pollen and homemade Salted Popcorn Ice Cream. To complement the elevated look and taste, Red Light has curated energetic, “Red Light has always been about bringing people together over exceptional drinks in an inviting, unpretentious environment. Our new location gives us the space to realise that vision fully, with the same soul and now a proper home for cocktails, food, and great music.”

candidates.evidence_text: The £35 million project set within 154 acres has transformed the former site of Worsley New Hall, restoring the historic walled garden, lake and surviving buildings Originally built for the 1st Earl of Ellesmere between 1840 and 1845, Worsley New Hall was a grand Gothic-style mansion, complete with glorious, formal landscaped gardens It’s now one of UK’s must-see gardens with so much to enjoy for visitors of all ages Step inside the magnificent 11-acre Weston Walled Garden, the site’s jewel in the crown. One of the largest Victorian walled gardens in the UK, it showcases a range of growing techniques and edible plants There’s also the spectacular Paradise Garden showcasing exotic planting inspired by Asiatic and Mediterranean gardens. The orchard and nearby bee and butterfly garden, have been designed to attract wildlife The Peel Learning Garden, supported by The Peel Group, will help schoolchildren learn how plants affect our lives and the planet, whilst the Community Wellbeing Garden provides a space for people to garden, socialise and relax

candidates.evidence_text: L-R: Simon Shaw, Anna Dick, Alastair Brown, Tripti Anil, Alan Jackson Simon Shaw, Delivery Director at Codurance, hosted the lunchtime session for tech leaders and introduced Codurance, which is a global software engineering consultancy that has run its Manchester office for 15 years He was joined on the panel by Anna Dick, Chief Technology & Product Officer at Capsule; Alastair Brown, Group Director of AI and Technology at Peninsula; Tripti Anil, Senior Leader, Data & Analytics at Kellanova; and Alan Jackson, Director of Client Solutions at Codurance Talking about discovering how AI can be used in projects, Anna said that Capsule's initial three months of AI exploration across all its business teams built appetite for further experimentation, but it also got a little out of control. Some things needed revisiting and tidying u Alastair stressed product discipline in order to understand the business driver and the outcome you want. At Peninsula, one initiative focused on giving customers richer answers and delivered over £1m in revenue. He said success depends on strong sponsorship and expertise from wi Tripti described spending three years building data foundations at Kellanova, focusing on "the right things at the right time" and bringing business teams along on the journey. They started with UK field sales as a proof of concept initially

candidates.evidence_text: It’s been a busy week at Labour Party Conference in Liverpool, with technology, growth and devolution featuring heavily in many of the conversations we’ve been part of In his first Conference speech as Prime Minister, Andy Burnham talked about devolving more power to places, backing businesses to grow and taking some of what has worked in Greater Manchester into a wider national approach. He also confirmed that AI will be a central focus of the That felt particularly relevant following an event we hosted through the UK Tech Cluster Group with AI Minister Kanishka Narayan, North East Mayor Kim McGuinness and other regional leaders, looking at AI, devolution and local growth One of the clearest themes from the discussion was that devolution should not mean every place trying to build the same thing. Different regions have different strengths, assets and specialisms, and there was a strong view that greater collaboration between places could create bi Procurement and buying local also featured strongly. The discussion highlighted the role public sector buying power can play in supporting regional businesses, helping successful pilots move into commercial contracts and strengthening UK capability in areas such as AI and cyber There was also a broader conversation about sovereignty and the UK’s role internationally. The discussion was not about trying to own every part of the AI stack, but about understanding where the UK already has genuine capability and where it makes sense to build more. Strengths

candidates.evidence_text: Teetotal dating goes fee-free at SoberLove - Prolific North Skip to content Tech Manchester insurtech closes £1m debut funding round TV, Film & Streaming Trailer drops as Coogan, Brydon and Winterbottom reunite for Trip to the Northern Lights Brand What’s gnu? Altrincham agency spearheads Typhoo Tea relaunch Teetotal dating goes fee-free at SoberLove Brand by Chris Newbould October 26, 2026 Manchester-founded teetotal dating app SoberLove is throwing open its doors to singles across the UK and beyond by making its dating platform completely free to join, with subscription fees removed to make alcohol-free romance more accessible than ever. The announcement comes as NHS figures reveal that an estimated 11.2 million adults in England have not drunk alcohol in the past year, and just days before founder Nicky Wake celebrates two years sober. Whether you’re sober, sober-curious, taking a break from drinking or simply tired of the expectation that every first date should involve a glass of wine, finding someone who shares your outlook on alcohol is becoming easier. Founded in Manchester in 2025 by dating app guru Wake, who also created the Chapter 2 and Widow’s Fire apps, SoberLove has already attracted around 4,000 registrations, and the platform is now removing its membership fees to encourage more singles to join and connect. READ MORE: Last chance to enter the Prolific North Tech Start-ups to Watch list 2026 The move comes amid changing social attitudes towards alcohol – the NHS Health Survey for England 2024, published in January 2026, found that 24% of adults in England, approximately 11.2 million people, had not consumed alcohol in the previous 12 months, up from 19% in 2022. Among 16 to 24-year-olds, the figure was approximately 35%. Yet dating can still be challenging for people who don’t drink, from explaining sobriety to a potential partner to navigating first-date nerves without alcohol. SoberLove offers an alternative, connecting people who share similar lifestyles and understand that romance doesn’t need to revolve around pubs, bars or drinking. For Wake, making SoberLove free is a deeply personal decision. In 2017, her husband Andy suffered a catastrophic cardiac arrest at home, leaving her desperately performing CPR while their nine-year-old son watched. Although Andy survived, the resulting brain injury was so severe that he no longer recognised his wife or child. For three years, she lived with the heartbreak of losing the husband she knew while he was still alive, before Andy died in 2020. Widowed and raising their son alone, she struggled with overwhelming grief and alcohol dependency, eventually reaching crisis point with an A&E admission and rehab in November 2024. On 6 November 2026, she will mark two years sober, having transformed her experiences into a mission to help others rebuild their confidence, relationships and lives without alcohol. Wake said, “When you’ve been through addiction and recovery, the thought of dating again can be terrifying. So much of our social lives revolves around alcohol, and it can feel as though you’re the odd one out simply because you don’t want a drink. I wanted to create somewhere people could meet without having to explain themselves, worry about being judged or feel pressured to compromise their sobriety. “In just a few days, I’ll be celebrating two years sober, something that once felt almost impossible. I know what it’s like to lose the person you love, to feel completely alone and to wonder whether you’ll ever find happiness again. There was a time when I couldn’t imagine a future without my husband, let alone a life without alcohol, but I’ve learned that even after the darkest experiences, it is possible to rebuild your life and find hope again. “That’s why making SoberLove free means so much to me. Nobody should face another barrier when they’re trying to find someone who understands their lifestyle. Whether you’re newly sober, have been in recovery for years or simply don’t enjoy drinking, you deserve the chance to find love, connection and happiness without feeling that you have to change who you are. “You don’t need a glass of wine to have chemistry, and you don’t need alcohol to fall in love. Some of the most meaningful connections happen when you’re completely yourself. If SoberLove helps someone feel less alone, find their confidence again or meet somebody who truly understands them, then everything we’ve been through to create it will have been worth

Screenings run at 10.30am, 11.30am For families keen to venture further into the cosmos, Horrible Science: Cosmic Chaos takes visitors on a mischievous voyage around the Solar System, combining interactive challenges, hands-on experiments and familiar characters from the BBC children’s series. Recast in a contemporary world of dynast As he shuffles irreversibly into decay and fateful paranoia, Lear mistakes flattery for loyalty and the allure of inheritance for unconditional love from his cynical children, setting in motion an excruciating chain of betrayals that leaves both kingdom and family in ruins. Mercury-prize There is a marked poignancy to seeing Threlfall and Dunster return to a theatre with which they share such a rich history, and King Lear makes an apt centrepiece for the Royal Exchange’s landmark anniversary year. candidates.evidence_text: A new exhibition at The Portico Library explores feminist themes of wellbeing, ageing and place in relation to magic and ritual healing Open now, Witches & Healers draws on Rosie Reed Hillman’s groundbreaking project Something That Was Ours , which explores what it means to be a witch today Hillman’s portraits of witches and healers are curated in dialogue with historic texts chosen by critical friends who identify with the practice of witchcraft and/or healing. The portraits, the books chosen, and their interpretation offer unique insights into the diverse lives an Using a mix of moving image and photography, the artwork builds a sensory and emotive portrait of women in midlife. Covering themes of menopause, mental health, climate change, and marital breakdown, this work explores the ways women have reclaimed the word witch and sought solac Speaking about the exhibition , Rosie Reed Hillman says: “I have worked to build rapport with contributors over the last four years and believe the intimate access conveyed in this project creates an exhibition that inspires empathy, curiosity and a greater understanding of issue “Women in midlife of all backgrounds are an overlooked demographic who want to see art and hear stories that reflect their experiences, and I hope this work speaks to them especially.”

candidates.lead: Bolton Car Boot Sale at Bolton Car Boot Sale
candidates.evidence_text: Bolton Car Boot Sale is one of the North West's biggest weekly boot sales, held in the hardstanding car park of the Macron Stadium (formerly Reebok), Burnden Way, Horwich, Bolton BL6 6JW. It runs every Sunday from February right through to December, drawing over 300 sellers and thousands of bargain hunters each week. Sellers can arrive and set up from 6:00 AM, with buyers welcomed in from 7:00 AM. Entry costs just £1 per car for buyers. Pitches for sellers are £14 for a car, £20 for a van and £3 for a trailer, with regular and corner pitches available on request. Bring exact change to keep the queue moving, and call organiser Andrew on 07470784644 for more details. Expect hundreds of stalls across the concrete hardstanding pitches, so it goes ahead in most weather. On-site you'll find a 5-star catering service, doughnuts and coffee, ice cream and desserts, a meat auction, fresh fruit and veg, plants, and retro sweet stalls. The sale is dog-friendly, has male and female toilets, ample parking, and kids' rides and bouncy castles to keep little ones entertained. Его путь начался в многонациональном Сараеве, где восточные мотивы естественно переплетались с западными традициями, а каждая улица имела свой ритм. Именно эта атмосфера сформировала композитора, впоследствии воз Впоследствии музыка Бреговича вышла за рамки концертных площадок. Сотрудничество с режиссером Emir Kusturica подарило мировому кинематографу саундтреки, ставшие неотъемлемой частью фильмов Time of the Gypsies, Arizona Dream и Underground. В этих мелодиях живут Балканы — с их своб Популярность Бреговича родилась не только благодаря знаменитым композициям “Kalashnikov”, “Ederlezi”, “In the Death Car” или “Bella Ciao”. Его главный талант — превращать народные мотивы в современное искусство, не теряя их подлинной силы. Вместе с легендарным “Wedding and Funera Окунитесь в этот балканский водоворот прямо в самом сердце Лондона! Город, который веками принимал выступления и разные культуры со всех континентов, на один вечер станет местом встречи британской сдержанности и безудержной балканской страсти.
